title: Anthropic Just Filed for an IPO. At a Potential Trillion-Dollar Valuation, It May Be the Most Consequential Listing in a Decade.
excerpt: The maker of Claude confidentially filed with the SEC on Monday, beating rival OpenAI to the public markets. For NRI tech investors, this is the moment the AI bubble either validates itself or cracks.
body:
Anthropic, the San Francisco-based AI lab behind the Claude family of models, announced on Monday that it has confidentially filed a draft registration statement with the US Securities and Exchange Commission for a proposed initial public offering. The company did not disclose the number of shares to be offered or the price range, but at its most recent private valuation of **$965 billion** — set just last week in a $65 billion Series H round — a public listing could place Anthropic firmly in trillion-dollar territory.

The filing makes Anthropic the first major AI model developer to formally move toward public markets, edging ahead of rival OpenAI, which Reuters reported is also preparing a confidential filing in the coming weeks. SpaceX, which filed publicly last month, is expected to launch its roadshow on June 4 with a target valuation of **$1.75 trillion** and could begin trading as early as June 11.

## The Numbers Behind the Filing

Anthropic's trajectory has been extraordinary even by Silicon Valley standards. Founded in 2021 by former OpenAI executives Dario and Daniela Amodei, the company has raised capital at an accelerating pace:

- **February 2026**: Valued at $380 billion
- **May 2026**: Raised $65 billion at $965 billion post-money valuation
- **June 1, 2026**: Confidential IPO filing with the SEC

The Series H round was led by Altimeter Capital, Dragoneer, Greenoaks, and Sequoia Capital. Amazon Web Services remains a major infrastructure partner — Anthropic committed more than $100 billion to AWS technology in April for training and running its models.

In a signal of commercial momentum, Ramp's AI Index found that **Anthropic surpassed OpenAI in business adoption in May**, with 34.4 per cent of businesses using Claude compared to 32.3 per cent on OpenAI products. The crossover is significant: enterprise revenue is the metric that public market investors will scrutinise most closely.

## What This Means for NRI Tech Investors

For Indian diaspora investors with concentrated positions in US tech, the Anthropic IPO raises several strategic questions:

**Allocation risk.** Anthropic, SpaceX, and potentially OpenAI could collectively seek more than $200 billion from public markets in 2026. Goldman Sachs has predicted US IPO proceeds could hit a record $160 billion this year. That volume of capital demand could create temporary pressure on existing tech holdings as institutional investors rebalance to make room.

**Valuation scrutiny.** The confidential filing will eventually produce a public prospectus — the first concrete window into how much revenue Anthropic actually generates, what its margins look like, and how fast it is growing. Private-market valuations of AI companies have been notoriously frothy. If the numbers disappoint, it could reset expectations across the AI sector, pulling down publicly traded AI infrastructure names like Nvidia, AMD, and cloud providers.

**The "first mover" advantage.** Analysts at IPOX noted that Anthropic benefits from filing shortly after SpaceX because it can "capitalise on strong investor interest in AI and growth stocks while the window remains favourable." The risk for investors is that appetite may cool after one or two mega-IPOs. If you are considering participating, earlier listings historically price better than the third or fourth in a wave.

**Index inclusion effects.** At a trillion-dollar valuation, Anthropic would immediately qualify for S&P 500 inclusion after meeting profitability and public-float requirements. Index funds — which now manage more than $15 trillion — would be forced buyers. For NRI investors already heavy in S&P 500 index funds, this means indirect exposure is coming whether you buy the IPO or not.

## The Broader AI Market Context

The filing lands during a week when Nvidia surged 6 per cent on the RTX Spark announcement, Microsoft climbed 2.3 per cent, and the S&P 500 set a fresh record to extend its winning streak to potentially ten consecutive weeks — the longest since December 1985. Software stocks, battered earlier this year on "SaaSpocalypse" fears, rallied after Jensen Huang declared at Computex: "This is actually an incredible time to be a software company."

But Brent crude also spiked 4.2 per cent to nearly $95 a barrel after Iran halted negotiations with the US and threatened to fully close the Strait of Hormuz. The 10-year Treasury yield rose to 4.47 per cent. For the AI thesis to survive a rising-rate environment, the companies going public will need to show real revenue growth — not just projections.

## What to Watch

The SEC review of Anthropic's confidential filing will take several weeks. Investors should track three things:

**The prospectus financials.** Revenue, gross margin, and net burn rate will determine whether the $965 billion valuation holds at listing.

**OpenAI's response.** If OpenAI files within days of Anthropic, it could split investor attention and compress both valuations. If it delays, Anthropic gets the market to itself.

**The SpaceX roadshow.** If SpaceX's June 4-11 roadshow generates overwhelming demand, it validates the mega-IPO thesis and likely lifts Anthropic's prospects. If it stumbles, the entire 2026 IPO calendar recalibrates.

For NRI tech investors sitting on concentrated portfolios of Magnificent Seven stocks, the message is clear: the AI trade is about to get a price tag. Whether that price confirms the thesis or exposes the froth, the next six weeks will tell us.

*Sources: Anthropic SEC filing announcement (June 1, 2026); Reuters; CNN Business; Fox Business; The Times; Ramp AI Index; Goldman Sachs IPO forecast; Investopedia.*
